# Diffuse curvature excludes extreme rays of the compatible planar support cone

This is a structural consequence of the guarded source construction. It
contains no monotonicity assertion for mixed halfspace depth.

## The cone and statement

Fix a finite base P and its finitely many extreme anchored barycentric
representations. Consider families of planar convex support functions h_z
satisfying every Jensen inequality h_z>=sum_w p_w h_w. The family is closed
under coordinatewise addition and nonnegative scaling; addition is the
fiberwise Minkowski sum. Translational linearity can be quotiented out if
one wants a pointed cone.

Suppose every fiber is a positive planar convex body and at least one
curvature measure R_z=h_z+h_z'' has a nonzero nonatomic part. Then this
family is not an extreme ray, even modulo any translational linearity.
More strongly, there is a nonzero signed perturbation delta h with compact
normal support in an interval of length less than pi such that both
h+t delta h and h-t delta h are compatible support families for all small
t>0. The perturbation can preserve any prescribed finite list of continuous
linear functionals of the support functions.

## Proof

Let R=sum_z R_z^c, and r_z=dR_z^c/dR. Use the exact-contact/source-pattern
construction in candidate c7a0c159c6cf35f0, omitting
all cap constraints. It is worth recalling the required ingredients.
A Jensen gap g_a=q_a.h is nonnegative, Lipschitz, and has BV derivative.
Diffuse derivative locality on {g_a=0} gives q_a.r=0 R-almost everywhere
on that zero set. Thus, on a positive-measure stratum with fixed zero
pattern A and positive-coordinate pattern J, the vector r belongs to

    L={v:q_a.v=0 for a in A, v_z=0 outside J}.

Since sum r_z=1, this subspace is nonzero. Restrict to a positive-measure
level min_(z in J)r_z>=1/k and to a compact interval inside an open guard
where every inactive gap is uniformly positive. This gives a nonzero
nonatomic measure nu dominated by every R_z with z in J.

Choose any nonzero v in L. For a bounded signed density psi on nu, impose

    integral psi sin(theta)dnu=integral psi cos(theta)dnu=0.

The Green potential

    phi(theta)=integral_(a<=s<=theta) sin(theta-s)psi(s)dnu(s)

then vanishes, along with its first derivative, outside the compact guard.
Its curvature perturbation is phi''+phi=psi nu. Any prescribed finite
linear support constraints on delta h_z=v_z phi are additional homogeneous
linear equations in psi. Divide the source into more disjoint positive-mass
measurable sets than there are equations and choose psi piecewise constant.
Elementary homogeneous linear algebra yields a nonzero solution. The
potential is nonzero because its distributional curvature psi nu is nonzero.

Put delta h_z=v_z phi. The changed curvature measures are

    R_z +/- t v_z psi nu,

nonnegative for sufficiently small t by domination. Each active-pattern
Jensen gap is unchanged identically, since q_a.v=0. Every other gap remains
nonnegative by its strict guarded margin. Outside the guard there is no
change. Hence both signed perturbations are actual compatible convex
support families.

These directions are not scalar multiples of the original family modulo
translations. Choose z with v_z!=0. Its nonzero curvature change is supported
inside an interval shorter than pi. A nonzero curvature measure of a full
planar convex body cannot be supported in that interval: the curvature
measure satisfies integral u(theta)dR_z(theta)=0, whereas every unit normal
in such an interval has strictly positive scalar product with its midpoint
direction. Therefore R_z has nonzero mass outside the perturbation interval.
If delta h were a scalar multiple t0 h modulo translations, its curvature
would be t0 R in every coordinate; the unchanged outside mass forces t0=0,
contradicting the nonzero changed curvature. Thus the decomposition is
nontrivial and the original family is not an extreme ray.

## Exact limit of the conclusion

An extreme compatible family, if it exists in an appropriate normalized
compact convex class, can have only atomic curvature. This does not prove
that it has finitely many atoms. It also does not say a local minimum of
halfspace depth is an extreme ray: no needed concavity or monotonicity of
the depth objective under this decomposition has been established.
